feed.title: Re: Safer sighashes and more granular SIGHASH_NOINPUT

entry.title: Re: Safer sighashes and more granular SIGHASH_NOINPUT
entry.summary:
In multi-party protocols, the final participant to sign a transaction possesses knowledge of the total weight, particularly when fixed-size signatures are employed. This individual holds the power to complete the signing process and is generally incentivized to do so if they wish for the transaction’s success. However, there are conceivable asynchronous protocols where no definitive last signer exists, though such configurations are considered unconventional.
A potential risk arises when the final signer acts with malicious intent or indifference toward the transaction’s outcome. In these scenarios, this party could deliberately inflate the transaction’s weight before signing, thereby causing inefficiency or disruption. To mitigate such issues, maintaining the anti-malleability Script Code remains important in protocol design, serving as a protective measure against intentional bloating or other forms of signature manipulation.
While acknowledging that the practice of signing the transaction weight introduces challenges across various situations, providing this option offers greater flexibility. It is preferable to have the capability to sign the weight directly rather than being compelled to rely solely on anti-malleability Script Code or non-consensus relay policies to secure transaction integrity. This approach strikes a balance between practical security concerns and the need for adaptable protocol features.
